html:
The Alazapas were one of the many small hunting and gathering bands of northeastern Mexico, in what is now Nuevo León, Coahuila and Tamaulipas. Spanish writers of the 1600s list them among the peoples of the new province of Nuevo León.

Like the other groups often lumped together as Coahuiltecan, they lived by gathering mesquite beans, prickly pears and roots, and by hunting. Slave raids, forced labour on Spanish estates, mission life and epidemics broke them up as New Spain pushed north, and by the 1700s they had disappeared as a separate people. Little else is known about them.
